Notes: 718-475-5242 is the pantry manager, printed on their pantry page; 718-475-5100 is the JCC switchboard. They ask you to book so it is one-to-one and private.

Description: One of the biggest pantries in Queens. Wednesdays are for older people and people with disabilities; Saturdays are for everyone. They also help you sign up for food stamps while you are there.
Hours: Wed and Sat; check their page for times
Tags: food; pantry; snap; queens; seniors; disability; all-populations
Notes: Their old address riverfundny.org is a parked domain now; river.fund is the live site.

Description: Queens' largest neighborhood organization: job training and placement, help for older adults, counseling, child care and after-school, across about eighty sites in the borough.
Cost: Free or low-cost depending on the program

Description: Help getting a job, free tax filing, and a credit union that will open an account for you if a bank has turned you down. Built around the public housing developments in Queens.
Who Can Access: Anyone; built for public housing residents
Tags: jobs; money; taxes; banking; queens; public-housing; all-populations; also:money
Notes: Runs its own federally chartered credit union for people banks will not take.

Description: A number to call when someone you love is losing their memory. Somebody trained in dementia picks up, at any hour, and will talk through what is happening and what to do next. They also run over eighty free support groups.
Who Can Access: Anyone caring for or living with dementia in New York City
Tags: seniors; dementia; alzheimers; caregiver; memory; mental-health; all-populations
Notes: Was the Alzheimer's Association's New York City chapter; independent since 2015. Site moved from caringkindnyc.org to wearecaringkind.org.

Subcategory: Everyday things you run out of
Description: Pads and tampons are free by law in every City school building from grade 4 up, in every City shelter, and in City jails. They are meant to be in the bathroom, not behind a desk. If they are not there, call 311 and say so.
Who Can Access: Students in NYC public schools; anyone living in a City shelter; anyone in a City jail
Address / Location: Every NYC public school building, City shelter and City jail
Tags: period; menstrual; supplies; schools; shelter; youth; all-populations
Notes: Local Laws 82, 83 and 84 of 2016; the school requirement now runs from grade 4. Food pantries often carry them too — ask.

Description: A free line for anything going wrong at school: a suspension, special education that is not happening, a child in a shelter being kept out, a language barrier nobody is bridging. They know what the school has to do and will tell you.
Who Can Access: Any parent, student or caregiver in New York City
Languages: English; Spanish; Arabic; Bengali; Chinese; French; Haitian Creole; Korean; Russian; Urdu
Tags: school; education; suspension; special-education; disability; youth; shelter; immigration; all-populations; my child was suspended; suspended from school; expelled; also:disability
Notes: Covers students with disabilities, students in temporary housing, discipline, early childhood, foster care, English language learners and charter schools.

Description: Six pantries where you pick what you want off the shelf, stocked with halal meat and the food people in these neighborhoods actually cook. Run by a Muslim charity and open to anyone, whatever your religion.
Who Can Access: Anyone; their pages state they serve people regardless of race or religion
Address / Location: Flushing, Jamaica, Bronx, Brighton Beach and Midwood; see their page for the day each one opens
Hours: One afternoon or morning a week at each site
Tags: food; pantry; halal; muslim; queens; brooklyn; bronx; all-populations
Notes: Each site opens one day a week: Flushing Wed, Jamaica Thu, Bronx Sat, Brighton Beach Mon, Midwood Tue. Ask for extension 1116 or 1113 to reach somebody who can help with more than food.

Description: A walk-in center in Jackson Heights for people who look for work on the street or get paid in cash. Help when a boss does not pay, safety training for construction, English classes, and somewhere to stand that is not the corner.
Who Can Access: Any immigrant worker; no papers needed
